items.title: Smulyan interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2010
items.q: there was a band called the Philip Morris Superband, which was conducted by Gene Harris... And we went on the road for three months.

ctx.x: So you have to constantly juggle your on-the-road commitments with whatever you have at home, including your employment at home, your teaching, but also your family life and that whole end of things.

Well my teaching, at least that situation now, as long as I make the number of lessons that I have to get in by the end of the semester I can do that. Like I said I’m not full time. I think full time faculty — people who have full time teaching positions, the demands made on them are a lot more, in terms of going to meetings, and so I don’t have those demands on me. I have the freedom to come and go, which is kind of a nice balance. But you know, yeah, I was away a lot. I have a son who is 22 and a daughter who…

going straight from the airport to my son’s baseball game with my suitcase and my baritone. You know? Trying to catch the tail end of his game. And I think that was hard for him. I think it was hard for my kids to be away that much. I mean they told me — my family’s always supported me, they’ve always understood that this is what daddy does, or this is what my husband does, and I see how the very core of the existence as a musician enabled me to be really great and supported in terms of my coming and going, but I…
